minimal.README.md:
# Pocket sum
A local ESM arithmetic library; sum accepts two numbers. No web server, database, deployment or persistence is implemented. HTTP transport is an idea, not a shipped feature.
minimal.src/sum.mjs: export function sum(a, b) { if (typeof a !== 'number' || typeof b !== 'number') throw new TypeError('numbers required'); return a + b; }
minimal.test/sum.test.mjs: import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { sum } from '../src/sum.mjs'; test('sum', () => { assert.equal(sum(2, 3), 5); assert.throws(() => sum('2', 3), TypeError); });

mature.README.md:
# Ledger fixture
An established local ledger library with append and read operations. See docs/architecture.md and docs/decisions.md for current behavior and policies. The historical synchronous-only storage description is obsolete. Cloud replication remains planned, not implemented.
mature.src/ledger.mjs: import { appendFile, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'; export async function append(file, event) { if (typeof event.id !== 'string') throw new TypeError('id required'); await appendFile(file, JSON.stringify(event) + '\n'); } export async function read(file) { const text = await readFile(file, 'utf8'); return text.trim() ? text.trim().split('\n').map(JSON.parse) : []; }
mature.test/ledger.test.mjs: import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises'; import os from 'node:os'; import path from 'node:path'; import { append, read } from '../src/ledger.mjs'; test('ledger roundtrip', async t => { const root = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'ledger-fixture-')); t.after(() => rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })); const file = path.join(root, 'events'); await append(file, { id: 'a', amount: 3 }); assert.deepEqual(await read(file), [{ id: 'a', amount: 3 }]); await assert.rejects(append(file, {}), TypeError); });
mature.docs/architecture.md:
# Current architecture
The library uses asynchronous Node filesystem calls. Events are newline-delimited JSON in a caller-selected local file. No HTTP endpoints, authentication, concurrent-writer locking or remote replication exist. Event identifiers are checked, but amount values are not validated.
mature.docs/decisions.md:
# Accepted local policy
A caller owns file placement and backups. A single writer per file is required. Corrupt JSON is a visible read failure, not automatically repaired. Changing the event format requires a migration decision; no migration utility exists. CI and deployment targets have not been chosen.
